## Detailed entries

### Dover

- **Type:** City
- **Recorded status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2026-10-12, City Council adopted Ordinance 2026-14 by unanimous roll call (Sudler absent), on motion of Hall seconded by Anderson; official minutes page41.
- **Normalized date:** `2026-10-12` (exact)
- **Duration:** Eighteen months from the effective date, unless sooner repealed; Council may extend by ordinance upon findings that additional study remains necessary. Adopted text section3 states immediate effect upon adoption; section8 supplies the term. Later amendment, repeal or extension remains unchecked.
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `de-dover-undated`
- **Legal basis:** Ordinance 2026-14, reproduced as adopted in official October12,2026 Council minutes pages41-43, following September28 first reading. Section3 states immediate effect upon adoption. The dated adoption minutes supersede the older undated register status as evidence of the October12 action. The minutes include a mayoral approval statement on page44 but no handwritten execution signatures; separate signed/enrolled copy and later actions are not established.
- **What prompted it:** Multiple inquiries about 'Large Energy Use Facilities' (data centers meeting defined MW/load thresholds); city wants time to study electrical capacity, ratepayer cost allocation, infrastructure, land use, environmental standards, and economic impact before adopting permanent regulations
- **Affected projects:** None named; city officials said they have been approached about at least one small-to-medium data center project but declined to identify it.
- **Detailed status:** Official October12,2026 minutes record adoption of Ordinance2026-14 by unanimous roll call, Sudler absent. The reproduced text immediately pauses acceptance, processing, review and listed approvals for new Large Energy Use Facilities: at least75MW monthly maximum demand with at least85% load factor; at least100MW monthly instantaneous demand; or a defined NAICS518210 data center using or capable of using at least30MW monthly maximum demand. Complete pre-effective applications are stayed unless withdrawn; limited vested-right/takings exemptions require Council approval following City Manager recommendation. Section5 exempts listed public/institutional uses, existing industrial expansions below20% demand, routine maintenance, existing telecommunications, defined clean-hydrogen production and public-utility infrastructure. The term is18months unless sooner repealed, extendable by ordinance. This establishes the historical action/text, not uninterrupted current force; subsequent council actions, litigation and separate executed-copy verification remain open.
- **Outcome:** —

### HB 233 / HS 1 for HB 233 (153rd General Assembly)

- **Policy ID:** `de-hb-233`
- **Sponsor / party:** Rep. Frank Burns; Sen. Stephanie Hansen; Rep. Debra Heffernan; D
- **Recorded status:** Original HB 233 introduced 2025-06-30 and listed Lieu/Substituted 2026-05-21; House Substitute 1 for HB 233 signed 2026-08-26, 85 Del. Laws ch. 440, effective on enactment 2026-08-26. Current legal effect, subsequent changes and implementation remain unverified.
- **Provisions:** Enacted House Substitute 1 covers large energy use facilities under alternative 75 MW/85%-load-factor, 100 MW instantaneous-demand, or 30 MW NAICS 518210 thresholds, with aggregation and specified exclusions. Requires utility rate classifications and service/security agreements to allocate costs and protect reliability. The 180-day rate-filing deadline runs from finalization of Commission regulations, not enactment.
- **Mechanism / scope:** utility_large_load_restriction; utility_grid
- **Legal effect:** unknown
- **Effective date:** 2026-08-26
- **End condition and limitations:** —
- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://legis.delaware.gov/BillDetail/143381>)

### SB 205

- **Policy ID:** `de-sb-205`
- **Sponsor / party:** Sen. Stephanie Hansen; Sen. Nicole Poore; Rep. Frank Burns; Rep. Debra Heffernan; Rep. Eric Morrison; others; D
- **Recorded status:** 153rd General Assembly ended; official bill page describes final recorded status Out of Committee on 2026-03-11. The retained record identifies no enacted act for SB 205; the rendered bill page shows no floor roll-call records.
- **Provisions:** As introduced, required a Public Service Commission certificate to operate for facilities using 30 MW or more. Senate Amendment 1, introduced 2026-01-28, would change the threshold to 100 MW, frame the certificate as a transmission certificate, add distribution-company requirements, and add water-supply review.
- **Mechanism / scope:** other; unknown
- **Legal effect:** failed
- **Effective date:** —
- **End condition and limitations:** —
- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://legis.delaware.gov/BillDetail/142714>)

### SB 312

- **Policy ID:** `de-sb-312`
- **Sponsor / party:** Sen. Poore; Rep. Burns; Rep. Heffernan; Rep. Minor-Brown; others; D
- **Recorded status:** Signed and effective 2026-08-26 (85 Del. Laws ch. 447).
- **Provisions:** Amends Title 9, Title 22, and Title 29 of the Delaware Code relating to data centers. Prohibits state agencies, counties, and municipalities from entering into nondisclosure agreements that would restrict public access to information about potential or actual large-scale data center development (defined by reference to facilities capable of using 100+ MW), aiming to preserve local transparency and public input into data-center siting decisions.
- **Mechanism / scope:** reporting_disclosure; statewide
- **Legal effect:** unknown
- **Effective date:** 2026-08-26
- **End condition and limitations:** —
- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://legis.delaware.gov/BillDetail/143259>)
